review_method: Independent maintainer reading of pinned arxiv-v1 full-text PDFs for the seven R2 documents originally gathered for the IV package: abstract/introduction/problem-setup pages closely read, plus a full-page keyword scan (shift, out-of-distribution, test-time/test time, unlabeled, covariate, robust, adapt) with every hit read in context. No model transport calls, no network, no new papers, no source/corpus/public-asset/code/existing-audit edits, no score changes. The IV-scope tiers in private_literature_roles_candidates.json were NOT transferred.

task_binding.scope: A pretrained deterministic scalar regression model faces changed input distributions. Deployment has unlabeled target inputs and no source examples or target labels. Source preparation may retain a documented finite summary of aggregate statistics, not original source examples. Do not assume the model already provides a predictive probability distribution.
task_binding.resource_distinction: No scientific numeric source-summary ceiling; package runtime budgets are separate.

label_semantics.core: High-priority lineage or access-regime comparator; not necessarily directly applicable or mandatory.
label_semantics.background: Conceptual/mechanistic support for interpreting approaches and evidence.
label_semantics.confusable: Relevant near-neighbor with an important condition liable to be confused with the task; not irrelevant or invalid. Same value as the requested 'near_confusable' label; the existing schema string 'confusable' is kept for consistency with the two earlier SSA audits.
label_semantics.unrelated: NEW in this file: after reading the inspected text, no substantive role for this task's access regime was found. Not an error label: retrieving or reading such a paper is not automatically penalized, and a solver may still legitimately cite it for a clearly scoped tangential point. Surface vocabulary overlap is recorded per paper.
label_semantics.insufficient_evidence: Insufficient inspected evidence for a role, not a negative label.
label_semantics.alternatives: Other valid documents may cover equivalent evidence. No single document is mandatory.
label_semantics.uncertainty: Tier boundaries are discretionary; doc-2212.07677 (unrelated) and doc-2208.01066 (confusable) sit on the confusable/unrelated boundary.

evidence_location_contract.normalized_page_sha256: sha256 of the normalized page text encoded UTF-8 (convention re-derived and confirmed against private_ssa_lit_existing_three_review_v1.json doc-2204.13263 p3 before use)

evidence_location_contract.quotes: At most 25 whitespace-delimited quoted words per paper; paraphrases reflect inspected conditions, not exhaustive summaries.

labels.title: Dual IV: A Single Stage Instrumental Variable Regression
labels.confidence_basis: Task-relative judgment, not calibrated probability or performance.
labels.task_relation: Not a source-summary/test-time-adaptation comparator. DualIV estimates a causal structural function from labeled observational (X, Y) data plus instruments Z under unobserved confounding; it offers no mechanism for adapting a pretrained regressor to unlabeled shifted inputs.

conditions_and_limitations.access_regime: Estimation requires outcome Y, treatment X and instrument Z samples at training time; no deployment-time adaptation phase, no retained source summary, and no unlabeled target-input setting is described in the inspected text.
conditions_and_limitations.surface_overlap_risk: Shares scalar-outcome regression vocabulary (Y in R) and the notion that E[Y|x] differs from an interventional prediction. The interventional counterfactual-prediction target is a confounding/identification problem, not covariate shift between source and deployment inputs; conflating them would be a relevance error.
conditions_and_limitations.deterministic_scalar_fit: Outputs a deterministic real-valued function estimate, but this is incidental; it does not bear on unsupervised adaptation.
conditions_and_limitations.why_not_confusable: No inspected passage frames the method as handling a shift in input distribution at deployment; keyword scan found 'shift' only in 'supply cost shifter' (p7, demand-simulation instrument). Tier boundary is discretionary, but citing it as a test-time-adaptation method would be unsupported.

labels.title: What Can Transformers Learn In-Context? A Case Study of Simple Function Classes
labels.confidence_basis: Task-relative judgment, not calibrated probability or performance.
labels.task_relation: Near-neighbor for 'regression predictor facing shifted inference-time inputs without parameter updates', but the mechanism consumes labeled input-output pairs in the prompt, which the task's deployment regime (no target labels) does not provide.

conditions_and_limitations.access_regime: In-context learning conditions on in-context examples that are input-output pairs; at deployment the task has unlabeled target inputs only. The robustness results therefore do not transfer to label-free adaptation.
conditions_and_limitations.shift_types: Studied shifts are (i) training-prompt vs inference-prompt distribution and (ii) in-context examples vs query input (e.g., skewed covariance, orthants, query scaling in Appendix B.1). These are genuine input-distribution shifts for a scalar-output model, which is why it is liable to be cited as test-time adaptation.
conditions_and_limitations.model_regime: Transformers are trained from scratch on synthetic function-class prompts; not a fixed pretrained regressor adapted with a source summary. No source-statistic retention is involved.
conditions_and_limitations.deterministic_scalar_fit: Outputs are scalar predictions without a predictive distribution, matching that task condition, but this does not make it an applicable adaptation method.
conditions_and_limitations.evidence_boundary: Synthetic linear/sparse/decision-tree/two-layer-network function classes; robustness is compared to least squares with the same labeled context. Citing it as evidence that a pretrained regressor self-adapts to unlabeled shift would overstate it. Tier boundary vs unrelated is discretionary.

labels.title: Transformers learn in-context by gradient descent
labels.confidence_basis: Task-relative judgment, not calibrated probability or performance.
labels.task_relation: Shows trained linear self-attention implements gradient descent on an in-context regression loss. Its out-of-distribution validation tasks rescale inputs/teacher weights while still supplying labeled in-context data; it is not a label-free adaptation method or a source-summary comparator.

conditions_and_limitations.access_regime: In-context data are labeled regression pairs; the implicit GD step uses those targets. The task's deployment has no target labels.
conditions_and_limitations.shift_content: OOD tests (p7, App. A.1/A.4) vary the input range U(-alpha, alpha) or scale teacher weights for validation tasks and compare Transformer vs GD degradation. This is shift in the in-context task distribution, not adapting a fixed pretrained regressor to unlabeled shifted inputs.
conditions_and_limitations.boundary_uncertainty: Closer to 'confusable' than the other ICL-mechanism papers because it reports input-range shift for regression; kept unrelated because shift robustness is a secondary validation of the GD-equivalence hypothesis and presupposes labels. A reviewer could reasonably move it to confusable; this is not a factual disagreement.
